topic: How do patient-specific instruments, navigation, and standard instrumentation affect source-reported glenoid positioning accuracy in shoulder arthroplasty?

pico.population: Human patients or cadaver shoulders undergoing anatomic or reverse shoulder arthroplasty with source-reported glenoid positioning measurements

intervention_or_exposure.description: Patient-specific instruments, navigation, or standard instrumentation for glenoid component positioning

comparison.description: Any source-reported glenoid positioning method or comparator

pico.outcome: Planned-versus-achieved glenoid version, inclination, starting-point, or offset deviation

targets.outcome: Source-reported planned-versus-achieved glenoid version, inclination, starting-point, or offset positioning summary
targets.comparison: Any source-reported glenoid positioning method or comparator; preserve arm labels and do not invent a comparator
targets.population_or_subgroup: Human patients or cadaver shoulders undergoing anatomic or reverse shoulder arthroplasty

timepoint_policy.rule: Use the report's planned-versus-achieved implant-position assessment and preserve the source-reported measurement method.

targets.effect_selection_rule: Capture every source-reported glenoid positioning axis, measurement semantics, unit, arm labels, and signed values. Do not calculate MD or SMD during extraction.
extraction_notes: Do not create a comparator for a single-arm summary.
Do not discard version, inclination, starting-point, or offset data because only downstream analysis decides the eligible axis.

primary_analysis_spec.outcome_group: absolute deviation from intended glenoid version
selection_rules: Select a calculator-complete patient-specific-instrument versus standard-instrumentation comparison.

Source selection: Capture every source-reported glenoid positioning axis, measurement semantics, unit, arm labels, and signed values. Do not calculate MD or SMD during extraction.
